## Current Phase

**Pre-release hardening.** The platform is built and integrated (Stripe, Checkr, Linq messaging, Twilio Video, Firebase, Evia). Focus is now correctness, single-source-of-truth, and closing the gap between what the docs claim and what runs end-to-end.

## Current Goal

Adopt the spec-driven workflow (these `context/` files), make type-safety actually enforced, and verify the release-gating success criteria in [project-overview.md](./project-overview.md).

- **2026-10-07 (LIVE: SUBMIT hours answered with a raw "6 ALREADY_EXISTS: Document already exists: …billingApprovalOutbox/…:approval-request:v1"; BUILT, UNCOMMITTED, functions — awaiting the founder's word).** Founder's screenshot (Evia submit-hours flow, 8:27 PM); the logs show the SAME failure from the site's own Submit callable at 04:26Z on a second shift ("Unhandled error" → the page toasted "internal"). Cause: `createValidatedShiftHours` created the family's approval-request outbox doc with `transaction.create`, keyed `{shiftId}:approval-request:v1`; the timesheet doc (`shiftHours/{shiftId}`) was gone while that outbox doc still existed, so a fresh submission collided. How the orphan arises: Reset Account sweeps field-keyed collections by clientId / userId / uid / recipientId / ownerId / requesterId / caregiverId — the outbox doc's key field is `recipientUid`, so a reset deletes the timesheets and leaves every approval-request doc behind (both shifts tonight had been submitted earlier today). FIXES: (1) the outbox write is `transaction.set` on both paths — a fresh submission is a fresh request (state back to pending, counters reset; the family gets this submission's approval text); (2) Reset Account's KEY_FIELDS gains `recipientUid`; (3) Evia's submit step texts only the callable's own message (the page's toast) — a gRPC-shaped error (numeric code / document path / "6 ALREADY_EXISTS:" prefix) becomes "I couldn't submit those hours just now. Please try again in a minute, or submit them from your Timesheets page." and is logged. Tests: orphan outbox → submission succeeds + outbox pending; reset sweep queries billingApprovalOutbox.recipientUid; flow texts the generic line for a raw error and the message for a refusal.   Root cause, found directly in code: every one of the file's 9 step handlers followed the same pattern — extract with a raw direct `getSharedClient().messages.create()` call (bypassing the project's shared `parseWithClaude`/`quickComplete` helper), and on ANY unrecognized or failed extraction, silently substitute a hardcoded default (`["Monday","Wednesday","Friday"]` for days, `["morning"]` for time, `["Companionship"]` for care needs, `"moderate"` for care level, rate defaulting to flexible on any non-numeric parse) and announce that default as if it were the user's real, confirmed answer — with no re-ask, no signal anything went wrong. A correction attempt is neither a recognized question (so the `isQuestionOrOther` guard doesn't catch it) nor a valid answer to the current question, so it fell straight through into this same defaulting path every time. Separately, the start-date extraction prompt never told the model what today's actual date was, so any relative date ("next Monday") was pure guesswork.
  Fix: every step now re-asks (with a distinct "Sorry, I didn't quite catch that" prefix) instead of substituting a fabricated default when a parse fails or comes back unrecognized — nothing merges or advances until a real, recognized answer lands. The start-date prompt now includes the real current date and day-of-week (Pacific time). Also reordered the entire flow to match the site's actual step sequence — confirmed via `PostJobFlow.tsx`'s component order and the wizard's own "Step 2 of 6" label — after an intermediate self-caught mistake of building who/where BEFORE schedule instead of after: **frequency → start date → days → time → who's it for → how many caregivers → which address → care needs → hourly rate → job title → description → confirm**. `jobCareLevel` ("light/moderate/full care") is no longer its own question at all — grepped the site's own wizard and confirmed it has NO input control anywhere that ever sets this field (display-only on the final review screen) — now derived automatically from care needs via the same `deriveCareLevel` helper the onboarding job-posting path already uses, matching the site's real behavior of never asking.

Rewired `buildJobPost.ts` (the finalization writer) to actually consume this per-job selection instead of only ever deriving from the stale onboarding-time snapshot: `caregiversNeeded` now actually reaches the public job listing (previously silently dropped); a genuinely new recipient or address gets appended to the account's persistent roster (`job_postings.additionalRecipients`/'savedLocations`, `carePlans.locationPool`) the same additive way the site's own `PostJobFlow.tsx` does (`arrayUnion`, "set primary only if none exists yet") — never overwritten/shrunk to match one job's narrower pick; `carePlans.locationPool` itself was previously overwritten down to a single entry on every job post (a pre-existing bug, fixed in the same pass since it directly undermines "pick from a previously-saved address" working at all).
  **Job title, added after Hamse flagged it directly** ("it should never be [auto-generated] care for the recipient, it has to match as the site"): confirmed via `Step5Describe.tsx` that the site auto-suggests "Senior care in {city}" but always lets the family type their own (10-80 chars) — `buildJobPost.ts` was instead silently manufacturing "Care for {name}"/"Light Care for {name}" with no way for the family to ever see or approve it.   Root cause, found by tracing the exact sequence: `approvalHandler.ts`'s `executeConfirmedAction` calls `claimPendingAction()` first (an intentional single-fire transaction that flips the pending doc's status `awaiting → executing`, guarding against a duplicate "yes" double-dispatching), THEN dispatches to the tool with `_confirmedActionId` set. But the MCP gate (`mcp/server.ts`'s `handleToolCall`) re-validates that confirmation via `isConfirmedActionValid()` (`pendingActions.ts`), whose valid-status check only accepted `"awaiting"` or `"approved"` — **never `"executing"`**. Since the claim always runs before the gate check, the gate always saw `"executing"` and always rejected. This is not probabilistic or LLM-dependent — it is a deterministic, 100%-reproducing bug that has affected **every single confirmed high-risk/irreversible action in the whole product** since this mechanism was built: `cancel_job_post`, `remove_family_member`, `delete_account`, `cancel_subscription`, 'set_block_status` (block/report), `create_refund_request`, `delete_review`, `archive_senior_profile`, `review_shift_hours` approve, and `respond_to_job_application` reject (the one that surfaced it).

  **Fix**: `isConfirmedActionValid` now also accepts `"executing"` (`pendingActions.ts`) — `claimPendingAction`'s own transaction (which checks 'status !== "awaiting"` before claiming) is what actually prevents a duplicate dispatch; this check exists to catch a forged/expired/wrong-tool/wrong-phone/tampered-input confirmation id, not to re-police a claim that already legitimately succeeded. (not the failure ack). This is the first test anywhere that exercises the full real confirmation round-trip rather than one half with a hand-seeded shortcut.

  **This is the headline fix of the session** — a live, reproducible, product-wide bug where saying "yes" to literally any high-risk confirmation prompt from Evia always failed.      - Hardened `HANDOFF_GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (`humanHandoff.ts`): claims about a scheduled item's current date/time/status, or a caregiver's current availability, are no longer ratable SUPPORTED on RECENT CONVERSATION consistency alone — they require TOOL RESULTS THIS TURN or the CURRENT MESSAGE, even if Evia said the same thing earlier this chat.

     Known gap surfaced but NOT fixed this session: `interviewIdentityGuard`'s check runs on `reply` AFTER the human-handoff grounding check may have already swapped it to the generic handoff copy — so a wrong-caregiver mismatch could slip past the identity guard in that specific ordering. No live harm seen (the live test's caregiver targeting was correct), but it's a latent risk, not yet fixed.
  4. **New capability, not a parity fix: proactive "did the interview happen?" nudge.** Neither the website nor Evia previously followed up on an `accepted` interview whose 'scheduledTime` had passed (the site's only path is a manual "Mark as Completed" button). A "yes" reply routes through Evia's normal turn handling, which already has `complete_interview`. Since CONTEXT (`buildClientCoreContext`) is freshly re-fetched from Firestore at the start of every single turn — not carried over stale from earlier in the conversation the way RECENT CONVERSATION is — excluding it was wrong and would have silently undermined the very fix just made (the new INTERVIEWS section would never have been enough on its own to satisfy the grounding gate for a schedule_appointment claim). Deployed and verified via `firebase functions:list`: the 6 broken callables are gone, `v1-processAccountActionQueue` (trigger) and `v1-expireAccountRecoveryRequests` (scheduled) are both live. Also ran `firebase deploy --only hosting` standalone to confirm the frontend deploy (the combined deploy's output didn't clearly show it). 292 functions test files / 3569 tests green (8 new for the trigger dispatcher). - **2026-08-31 (real production bug, found by Hamse live-testing: a fact-correction detector hijacking totally unrelated questions — PROMPT FIX ONLY, deployed indexes unaffected, CODE COMPLETE, full suite green, NOT yet committed/pushed/deployed).** Hamse hit a run of plain questions — "Is my account approved", "Can you check if my membership is active", "Do I have a shift coming up", "Are you sure" — each answered with a completely unrelated, jarring reply: "I checked what I have remembered, and I can't identify that memory, so I haven't changed anything. Could you tell me what I said that needs fixing?" Traced to `functions/src/memory/learnedFacts.ts`'s `detectAndStageFactChange` — every single user turn (any role, gated only on identity being confirmed) is checked by an LLM call asking "does this message correct or ask to forget one of the family's stored facts?", and the (cheap-tier) model was sometimes answering `{"noMatch":true}` for messages that are plainly just questions, which returns the confusing canned reply and skips answering the real question entirely — the most disruptive failure mode of any bug found tonight, since it silently derails the whole turn rather than just giving a wrong answer.
  This one is architecturally different from tonight's other fixes: CLAUDE.md's own rule for this codebase is "intent/meaning must be judged by an LLM, never a regex/keyword list" — so unlike the medical-refusal bug, there's no hard, deterministic safety-net override available here without breaking that rule. Fixed the only way available under that constraint: substantially rewrote the detection prompt with explicit counter-examples (the exact phrases that misfired) and an explicit instruction to default to "not a correction" whenever genuinely unsure, since a false "can't find that memory" derailment is worse than silently missing an edge-case correction. **Honest caveat, unlike tonight's other fixes**: this can't be given the same regression-test guarantee — it depends on how the model actually responds to the improved prompt at runtime, not something a mocked unit test can prove. Existing 42-test suite in `learnedFacts.test.ts` still green (unaffected — none of it asserts on prompt wording). Full suite green (288 files, 3540 tests).

- **2026-08-31 (two more real production bugs from Hamse's live-testing: a misfiring medical-refusal block, and a caregiver-matching flow that never used real distance/eligibility — CODE COMPLETE, full suite green, NOT yet committed/pushed/deployed).** Hamse shared two more real conversations: (1) "Can you find me caregiver near me" got a hardcoded refusal — "Evia coordinates non-medical care and cannot search for providers..." — a message meant only for actual medical-provider requests (doctors/pharmacies), firing on Evia's own core job; (2) repeatedly asking for "any more caregivers" always re-suggested the same single caregiver (Imran), and two caregivers visible on the website's Browse Caregivers page never appeared through Evia at all.
  1. **Medical-refusal misfire**: traced to `functions/src/agents/intentClassifier.ts` — an LLM classifies each message into an intent bucket, and "find me a caregiver near me" has the same sentence shape as "find a cardiologist near me," so it sometimes got mislabeled `FIND_NEARBY_PROVIDER` (medical-only) instead of `FIND_CAREGIVER`. `functions/src/linq/routeIntent.ts` then hard-deflects on that label with a canned refusal, before Evia's real caregiver tools ever run. Fixed: tightened the classifier's own prompt with an explicit two-way disambiguation, and added a safety net — a new exported `isCaregiverSearchMisroutedAsProviderSearch()` in `intentClassifier.ts` that always overrides the medical-refusal path when the message literally says "caregiver," regardless of what the model guessed.
  2. **Matching used a fake distance and incomplete eligibility, unlike the site**: `functions/src/agents/matchingAgent.ts` (`runMatchingForClient`, used both by the direct caregiver-search intent and the `find_replacement_caregivers` tool) filtered candidates by exact city-string match or matching zip-code prefix — a crude proxy, self-documented in the old code as "no lat/lng in this flow" — and only checked 'status`, never the site's real bookability rule (`onboardingStatus`+`verificationStatus`). The website's own "Nearby Caregivers" logic (`caregiverMatchScoring.ts`, already byte-ported from the frontend, already used by a sibling Evia action) does real haversine distance + the canonical `isCaregiverBookable()` check. Fixed: `matchingAgent.ts` now geocodes the client's location once (`geocodeCityOrZip`, already existed) and uses real `haversineDistanceMiles` for both the candidate-pool radius filter and the rule-based distance score, plus post-filters every candidate with `isCaregiverBookable()` — falling back to the old proxy only when a coordinate is genuinely missing on one side. Deliberately deferred (Hamse's call): the separate bug where declined caregivers get re-suggested (a session/profile object mixup dropping `rejectedCaregiverIds`) and the missing "exclude this person by name" input — real, found, but not fixed tonight.
  New tests: `functions/src/agents/__tests__/matchingDistance.test.ts` (4 tests, real-distance calculation + fallback), `intentClassifier.test.ts` (+5 tests for the safety net). Full suite green (288 files, 3540 tests), root contract test green.

- **2026-08-31 (real production bug, found by Hamse live-testing: Evia honestly reporting a genuine backend failure, traced to missing Firestore composite indexes + one invalid query — CODE COMPLETE, full suite green, NOT yet committed/pushed/deployed).** Hamse shared a third live conversation: asked about upcoming shifts, Evia consistently (across 5 turns, including after "double checking") said "I can't access the live calendar right now." Unlike the two prior bugs tonight, this wasn't a hallucination — traced it to a real backend error: `get_upcoming_appointments`'s 'shifts` query (`clientId==, status in [...], date>=`, added in the 2026-08-30 booking-pipeline redesign) has no matching Firestore composite index, so it throws `FAILED_PRECONDITION` every time, and Evia was honestly reporting the failure. An Explore-agent audit of every multi-field query against 'shifts`/`booking_requests`/`appointments` across `functions/src` (46 tool calls) found this was one of ~20 affected call sites, several inside the scheduled reminder/nudge jobs already deployed earlier tonight (day-before reminders, 30-min reminders, morning briefings, weekly digest) — meaning those may be silently failing in production right now, since deploying functions and deploying Firestore indexes are separate steps and only functions went out. Also separately found: `upcomingVisitReminder.ts` passed `dateOp:"in"` with a 2-value array into `queryVisitsMerged`, which always adds its own 'status in [...]` filter — two `in` clauses in one query is outright invalid in real Firestore (not just a missing index), so that cron threw on every single run. Manually verified `chatRooms` (used by tonight's Messages/Inbox fixes) already has its required index — not part of this gap. Fixed: added 4 missing composite indexes to `firestore.indexes.json` ('shifts`: clientId+status+date, and a bare date+status; `appointments`: caregiverId+status+date ASC, and caregiverId+clientId+status — this last one also unblocks the caregiver-messaging relationship check in 'send_client_message`); changed `upcomingVisitReminder.ts` to a `>=`/`dateUpperBound` range instead of `dateOp:"in"` (today/tomorrow are consecutive dates, so the range covers the same window); added a permanent warning comment in `visitQuery.ts` against ever passing `dateOp:"in"` again. New regression test in `visitQuery.test.ts`. Full suite green (287 files, 3528 tests), root contract test green. **Important for the deploy step**: Firestore indexes deploy separately from functions (`firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`, or a full `firebase deploy`) — the earlier `--only functions` deploys tonight would NOT have picked up an index change even if one had been made then. Newly-created indexes also take real time to build after deploying (not instant) before queries against them stop failing.

- **2026-08-31 (real production bug, found by Hamse live-testing: Evia confidently denied having data it actually had, in two separate ways — CODE COMPLETE, full suite green, NOT yet committed/pushed/deployed).** Hamse shared two real SMS conversations: (1) asked "What is the care address"/"the favorite activity" — Evia denied having the address twice and denied lifestyle data twice, then on a third push ("can you double check") revealed it actually had the full street address AND a lifestyle note the whole time; (2) asked "Who is my caregiver" — Evia answered with the FAMILY MEMBER's own name, then said it "can't verify," then on a third push correctly named the real caregiver. Root cause investigated and confirmed via an Explore agent trace, two independent bugs:
  1. **Routing bug**: `isTrivialQuickReply` (`functions/src/agents/qaAgent.ts`) decided whether a message goes to the tool-less "quick reply" fast path or the full tool-having agent based on a list of specific topic keywords — any short question that didn't happen to contain one of those words (e.g. "What is the care address", "I think you do", "Are you sure") fell through to the fast path, which structurally cannot see most of what's on file. Fixed: replaced the keyword-list approach with detecting the *shape* of a real question (has "?", or starts with an interrogative word) or a factual pushback ("I think...", "that's not...") — this always escalates to the full agent regardless of topic, closing the whole bug *class*, not just these specific phrasings. A carve-out (`GREETING_QUESTION`) keeps genuine rhetorical greetings ("How's it going?") on the cheap fast path. This fix is universal — it's one shared gate every message passes through, so it protects every page already audited this session (and future ones) without needing per-page changes.
  2. **Stale "cheat sheet" bug**: `buildClientCoreContext` pre-loads a short summary at the start of every conversation so Evia doesn't have to re-fetch everything on every turn. Two of its five sections were quietly incomplete: the CARE PLAN section was hardcoded to only `["careNeeds","notes"]`, silently omitting `locations` (the real address) and `lifestyle` (preferences) even though they live on the same doc — and the label claimed "(full, on file)" when it wasn't. Separately, the CARE TEAM roster section only ever queried the legacy `appointments` collection — a caregiver relationship living entirely in the newer `booking_requests`/'shifts` pipeline (which `get_care_team`, the real tool, already correctly checks) was invisible here, so the ambient summary went empty/wrong and Evia guessed instead of calling the tool — this is confirmed to be exactly what produced the "your caregiver is you" answer. Fixed both: CARE PLAN now includes address + lifestyle (lifestyle formatted generically off whatever keys are actually present, not a hardcoded field list, so a future preference type can't cause this same class of bug again); CARE TEAM roster now merges both pipelines, deduped by caregiver name. Unlike the routing fix, this one is **not universal** — it only covers these two sections because those are the only two sections that exist in this pre-loaded summary; Bookings/Messages/Care Requests/Calendar have no equivalent ambient summary at all, so this bug class structurally cannot occur there (their correctness instead comes from the routing fix + each page's own already-audited tool).
  New tests in `functions/src/agents/qaAgent.test.ts` (added ~15 new cases across `isTrivialQuickReply`, the CARE PLAN section, and a new CARE TEAM roster describe block, including a regression test reproducing the exact "Basra Yousuf" scenario). Full suite green (287 files, 3527 tests), root contract test green.

- **2026-07-02** — **Durable retry queue for the two silent-drop outbound paths (`linq_outbound_queue`).** 'safeSend`/'sendToPhone` previously *discarded* messages when the Linq circuit breaker was open (line FLAGGED/CRITICAL) or the per-pair rate limit hit — a cancellation notice or APPROVE prompt sent during a line incident was simply lost, and `toolNotify.trySend` still reported `{sent:true}` (Evia would claim "I let them know" about a message that never went out). Now: blocked sends are parked in new server-only `linq_outbound_queue` (`functions/src/linq/outboundQueue.ts`) and drained by a new every-minute scheduled sweep (`v1-drainLinqOutboundQueue`, 'scheduled/outboundQueueDrain.ts`) — transactional claim (queued→sending, attempts++ at claim so crash-loops still cap out), exponential backoff (1m→10m cap), max 6 attempts then `failed` + high-severity `admin_alerts`, per-target oldest-first ordering (a blocked target's later messages are skipped that pass, never delivered out of order), chat-target messages re-run through 'safeSend` so they are re-supervised at delivery time (a chat doc with no supervise context is failed, never sent unsupervised). **Staleness classes:** every queued doc has an `expiresAt` — default 15 min for unmarked sends (a stale "running late" is worse than none), 6h must-deliver for `toolNotify.trySend` action notifications; expired docs are marked, never delivered late. Rate-limited sends become due at the next 60s window. `SendOptions` gains `durability:'queue'|'drop'` (default queue), `queueTtlMs`, 'source`; 'safeSend`/'sendToPhone` now return `GuardedSendOutcome` ('sent|queued|dropped|skipped_opt_out`) — `trySend` maps these honestly (`queued_for_retry`, `linq_line_unavailable`, `recipient_opted_out`; the opt-out silent-'sent:true` misreport is also fixed) and the qaAgent prompt tells Evia a `queued_for_retry` message will deliver automatically (no manual-retry offer). Enqueue failure degrades to the old drop behavior (fail-open, loud log). New composite index `linq_outbound_queue(status,notBefore)`; server-only firestore.rules block; EXCLUSIONS internal-infra row added. Tests: `linq/outboundQueue.test.ts` (enqueue timing/TTL/fail-open + drain deliver/expire/backoff/order/opt-out/final-fail-alert). Committed `35bcc0d` on `fix/cara-bug-hunt-2026-06-29`. **DEPLOYED 2026-07-02:** rules + indexes released, then full functions deploy (`FUNCTIONS_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=120`, no `--force` so nodejs20 orphans untouched) — 162 updates + `v1-drainLinqOutboundQueue` created, 0 failures; new function verified live via `functions:list` (scheduled, nodejs22).

## Session Notes

- Type-safety scope was chosen deliberately. Measured fallout: full 'strict` = ~253 Evia errors (187 null-safety); `noImplicitAny` alone = 52. Both would be large diffs with a red type gate, so instead we installed the *enforcement mechanism* green now (excluded `third_party`, fixed the 2 real bugs, added `typecheck` + build gate) and staged the strictness ramp as backlog item #1. A green gate today is worth more than a half-on 'strict` with 50â€“250 failing checks.
- Build pipeline note: `vite build` (esbuild) does NOT typecheck â€” `npm run typecheck` is the real type gate.
